newsitem.title: USA: Fall harvest glut pulls down farm price index.
newsitem.headline: Fall harvest glut pulls down farm price index.

text.p: A harvest-time downturn in corn, wheat, soybean and milk prices pushed down a key farm price index by 3.4 percent in October, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Thursday.

Milk prices hit a record high of $16.30 per 100 pounds in September but eased to $16 in October. The department attributed the decline to higher milk output and sharply lower butter and cheese prices.

The index, a gauge of prices paid to farmers for their crops and livestock, had an October reading of 112, down 3.4 percent from September, but still 7.7 percent higher than a year ago, when it was bolstered by strong grain, cattle and hog prices.
Soybean prices averaged $6.85 per bushel in October, down 94 cents from September.
"Harvest of new crop soybeans has been the major factor in the price decline," the department said. Prices for peanuts, sunflowers and cottonseed -- other sources of vegetable oils -- also fell.
Wheat fell 21 cents to average $4.16 a bushel and corn, at $2.91, was down sharply from September's average of $3.56 a bushel.
The fall harvest, which hit full stride in mid-September, was replenishing scanty U.S. stockpiles. Wheat prices fell, the department said, because of large overseas crops.
Beef cattle prices averaged $63.60 per 100 pounds in October, down 10 cents from the preceding month but $4.80 higher than a year earlier.
Hog prices rose $2.10 during October to average $56.80 per 100 pounds. Broiler prices fell to 40.6 cents per pound, down 0.8 cent.
Cotton was up slightly to average 72.2 cents per pound. Rough rice sold for $9.80 per 100 pounds, down from $9.95 in September.
